title: introduce-rate-match-autoscaler-and-util-fingerprint-telemetry
author: Evelyn Brooks
release_notes: Added a new rate-matching autoscaler mode that dynamically reconciles tenant throughput targets with observed request pacing; introduces a lightweight utilization fingerprint metric for more stable telemetry-driven decisions.
commits: a1b2c3d: introduce rate-match controller and reconciliation loop
d4e5f6a: add util_fingerprint telemetry aggregator and metrics export
b7c8d9e: add config flags, defaults, and unit tests for controller edge cases
f0e1d2c: update docs, integration test harness and rollout plan
description:
Problem: Tenant throughput guarantees currently rely on coarse concurrency targets and headroom heuristics which overreact to transient bursts or noisy utilization signals. This causes oscillation in Dedicated pools and uneven latency for tenants that have steady-rate workloads.

What this PR does: Implements a new 'rate-match' autoscaler mode for Dedicated capacity that focuses on matching observed served RPS to tenant-declared throughput targets (or inferred targets from historical steady-state windows). The controller adjusts two knobs: effective concurrency cap and burst-window allowance. It uses a short-term PID-like reconciling loop combined with a decay-based safety to avoid rapid oscillation.

Key features and rationale:
- Rate-matching policy: target_rps -> compute desired concurrency via adaptive estimator that accounts for median token-per-request and observed latency percentiles. This reduces unnecessary scale-ups when token costs fluctuate.
- Burst window control: instead of outright granting large static burst credits, tenants get a moving burst-window quota proportional to sustained utilization; soft-revert restores baseline over a configurable half-life.
- Utilization fingerprint: a compact 64-bit hash-like fingerprint (stable across short replays) that summarizes workload shape (median seq len, concurrency distribution, long-tail latency buckets). Fingerprint is exported to TSDB as a tag to group telemetry by workload-shape, making long-term regressions and model changes easier to detect.
- Signal smoothing: introduces an exponential smoothing layer and util-fingerprint-aware dampening so scale decisions weigh persistent shifts more than single-window spikes.
- Config: opt-in via fleet.autoscaler.mode="rate-match"; flags for burst_half_life, smoothing_alpha, and max_concurrency_delta_per_min. Default is conservative (off) and enabled gradually.

Files changed (high-level):
- pkg/autoscaler/controller/rate_match_controller.go (primary controller loop, reconciler)
- pkg/autoscaler/estimator/throughput_estimator.go (estimator functions and tests)
- pkg/telemetry/util_fp/agent.go (fingerprint builder + unit tests)
- internal/config/defaults.yaml (new defaults and flags)
- deploy/dedicated/helm/values-rate-match.yaml (example rollout config)
- test/integration/autoscaler_rate_match_test.go (integration tests with simulated tenants)
- docs/ops/autoscaler-rate-match.md (operator doc + rollback steps)
- scripts/bench/provision_small_cluster.sh (bench harness tweak)
- observability/dashboards/rate-match-overview.json (dashboard panels)

Testing and results:
- Unit tests: added for estimator corner cases, burst-window decay and fingerprint stability (coverage +6%).
- Integration: simulated 120 tenants with mixed steady / bursty profiles; rate-match reduced scale oscillation by 48% vs baseline step-autoscaler and improved median P95 latency by ~12ms for steady tenants under mixed load.
- Bench: small cluster stress run (30m) to validate no token-cache starvation.

Rollout plan: staged rollout across Dedicated fleets: canary (5% traffic) -> pool-wide (50%) -> full. Helm values provided for safe defaults. Auto rollback if P95 latency for any tenant increases by >20% for 15m and reconciler logs show >10 rapid adjustments per minute.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing autoscaler modes unchanged; rate-match is opt-in.
- Telemetry backward compatible: util_fingerprint introduced as optional metric tag; missing tag is treated as "unknown-fp" in dashboards.

Operational concerns:
- The fingerprint computation is cheap (O(1) per aggregate window) but we added CPU budget checks to avoid overhead at very high fleet cardinality.
- Safety nets: max_concurrency_delta_per_min prevents runaway concurrency changes; we retained existing emergency-fallback: fallback to step-autoscaler if reconciliation errors exceed threshold for 3 consecutive cycles.

Related work: ENG-9271 (autoscaler smoothing), ENG-9432 (observability gaps for tenant shaping).

Author notes: this PR is intentionally conservative: defaults keep behavior identical until operators enable rate-match. The code is contained to autoscaler and telemetry subsystems with minimal cross-cutting changes.
review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a debug endpoint that emits current fingerprint + raw histograms for a tenant to speed triage? (2) please add a small comment in estimator describing how median tokens-per-request is estimated under truncated traces.
Evelyn Brooks (reply): Added a /debug/tenant/:id/fp endpoint in controller and expanded estimator docs; also added a unit test for truncated traces.
Aisha Kaur: Telemetry looks good; make sure tag cardinality stays constrained. Suggest we bucket fingerprints into stable families in the dashboard rather than raw-fingerprints everywhere.
Samir Patel: Tested canary on staging. Observed one tenant that saw 2 rapid deltas due to very spiky traffic; recommend lowering default max_concurrency_delta_per_min to 5 for conservative rollout.
Evelyn Brooks (reply): Lowered default to 5 and documented the rationale in ops doc.
